semanticGuidePage.title: Semantic Guide
semanticGuidePage.description: How the five tones and the ADIE separation are applied across the interface.

tones.trust: Verified, healthy, validated. Used only when a positive assertion is backed by evidence.
tones.info: Informational, pending, proposed. Neutral state — not a judgment.
tones.warning: Review needed, degraded, stale. Signals caution, not failure.
tones.critical: Failure, attack, confirmed loss. Reserved for the highest severity.
tones.unknown: Not evaluated, unavailable, not connected. The honest default.

goldenRule.why: If a positive state has not been verified, the interface must say so. Substituting Trust for Unknown is the most dangerous lie a security UI can tell.
goldenRule.incorrectNote: Never render verified when the state is unknown.

adie.intro: The architecture separates four pairs of concepts that are often conflated. Each side answers a different question.

examples.pending: Use for work that is queued but not yet decided.
examples.unknown: Use when the state has not been evaluated. Never upgrade to trust silently.
examples.information: Use for neutral context that is neither good nor bad.
